name: Pennsylvania

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (5 Pa.C.S. ch. 35)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers endorsement deals, and a college athlete's NIL agent must act under it or be a Pennsylvania lawyer (24 P.S. 20-2004-M).
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) If you enter into negotiations for, or sign, a professional-sports-services contract, you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) If you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent shall notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (3) You may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it.
summary: Register with the State Athletic Commission. $200 plus a state police record check.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Application
Get a Pennsylvania State Police record check
steps.detail: Request it online through PATCH. The law requires it with your application.
$150 if you're registered in another state.

steps.text: Mail it to the State Athletic Commission
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you contact a minor's parent, or anyone you want to sway the athlete. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you're registered in Pennsylvania and list your other states. Add your pay and how it's figured, other pay you get for the deal, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: In a college NIL contract, say the athlete doesn't have to use you for anything else
steps.detail: Pennsylvania requires this line in any contract to find NIL deals for a college athlete.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete in bold in the contract
steps.detail: Use Pennsylvania's set wording. If the athlete is a minor, change it to speak to the parent.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: A parent or guardian signs it if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the warning when they sign
steps.detail: Give it to the parent if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell them too. The athlete (or parent of a minor) may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Tell the State Athletic Commission within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Pennsylvania makes both you and the athlete give the commission written notice of the contract.

steps.text: Tell the new school within 72 hours if your athlete enrolls later
steps.detail: Count from when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Pennsylvania and federal law (SPARTA) ban predating or postdating it.
Each client's name and address, each contract and what you spent to recruit each athlete. The commission may inspect them.

steps.text: Never mislead athletes or give them anything that could cost their eligibility
steps.detail: A gift is only OK if you tell the athletic director within 72 hours and the athlete signs a warning. Fines can reach $50,000.
Registration lasts 2 years. The renewal fee is $150 if you renew based on another state's registration.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: 5 Pa.C.S. 3511(i) says you must tell the commission about each contract within 72 hours. No form or address for this notice was found. Ask the State Athletic Commission how to send it.
The commission's phone number was not found on its athlete agent page. Find it on the State Athletic Commission page at pa.gov.
The step links go to single sections on palegis.us, which loads text with scripts. The full chapter was read in the official PDF on palegis.us.
